question: An 18-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents because he suddenly collapsed while playing football. His parents mention that he had complained of dizziness while playing before, but never fainted in the middle of a game. On physical examination, the blood pressure is 130/90 mm Hg, the respirations are 15/min, and the pulse is 110/min. The chest is clear, but a systolic ejection murmur is present. The remainder of the examination revealed no significant findings. An electrocardiogram is ordered, along with an echocardiogram. He is diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and the physician lists all the precautions he must follow. Which of the following drugs will be on the list of contraindicated substances?
analysis: In a patient diagnosed with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the use of drugs that can exacerbate the condition by increasing the heart rate or causing further myocardial oxygen demand should be avoided. Beta-blockers are the first-line treatment for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy as they reduce heart rate and improve diastolic filling time, hence they are not contraindicated. Dobutamine, a positive inotropic agent, should be avoided as it can worsen the condition. Potassium channel blockers can prolong the QT interval and increase the risk of arrhythmias, so they are contraindicated. Nitrates can cause vasodilation and hypotension, which may worsen symptoms in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Calcium channel blockers can also worsen symptoms by increasing myocardial oxygen demand and should be avoided.
